article.title: Titan posts 24% jewellery revenue growth and raises its store addition target
article.text: Titan Company reported twenty-four per cent year-on-year growth in its jewellery division against consensus of about fifteen, with studded share improving one hundred and ten basis points and same-store growth in the high teens across all four zones. Management raised the full-year store addition target from ninety to one hundred and thirty and said the studded mix improvement was structural rather than a festive artefact. The company also said gold customs duty changes had not disturbed its exchange programme economics. Kalyan Jewellers reports next week; brokerages were split on whether Titan's studded gain came at an organised-competitor's expense or from the unorganised trade.
article.note: The read-across trap: a strong print from one listed jeweller is not evidence about the next one, and the article itself says the analysts cannot tell where the share came from.

shocks.label: Jewellery demand beat
shocks.mechanism: A reported revenue beat with an improving studded mix raises the realised gross margin per transaction and validates a faster store rollout against the same fixed cost base

companies.name: Titan Company
companies.mechanism: Reported growth nine points ahead of consensus with a one hundred and ten basis point studded mix gain lifts both revenue and realised margin, and the raised store target extends it into the following year
companies.rationale: The company's own reported numbers and its own raised guidance

companies.name: Kalyan Jewellers India
companies.mechanism: Industry-wide organised jewellery demand implied by the leader's print should translate into a comparable same-store trend at the next reporting franchise-led retailer
companies.rationale: Read-across from the sector leader's reported quarter ahead of its own results

reject.reason: no real exposure to this shock: the article states the source of the share gain is unknown, so the leader's print is not evidence about this company's own quarter

ground_truth.rationale: A company's own reported numbers are the strongest evidence the system ever sees -- primary without qualification. The peer read-across is exactly the claim the article itself says cannot be made: if the share came from the organised competitor, the read-across has the SIGN BACKWARDS. Rejecting it is not conservatism, it is refusing to guess a direction.
